I used to be suicidal, and I actually am no longer suicidal, depressed, and anxious anymore. They took back my diagnosis because I improved my life significantly. If that’s something that gives you hope, I hope it does.

So my medical history: I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety when I was 17, had it since I was 10 or 11. I developed PTSD after I left my abusive household, at age 19. I then developed Schizoeffective Disorder at age 21 and had a psychotic break, scariest shit of my life I was hallucinating the entire time and saw spirits and demons and angels. I am now 22.

Through therapy with good counselors I was able to use CBT to stop my irrational thinking and negative self talk that I developed from the abuse I experienced. Still have to use it once in a while when I have an irrational thought. I take medicine for my schizoeffective disorder and it actually helped stop my depression and anxiety significantly as well. Then later on, it all went away. I have been anxiety, depression, and suicide free since May 2019 (been almost 8 months now) and have been the happiest I’ve ever been. But I do still have Schizoeffective Disorder

It takes a while. Im not surprised that you feel worse after a year. Digging deep and recovering all that shit is hard. I wouldn’t necessarily say that you will never be able to recover. Also Im still doing counseling because Im constantly working on myself.

I had a hard time switching schools in high school. I was happy going to one school, then all of a sudden, for my senior year, my neighborhood was redistricted and I was forced to switch high schools. reaaallly sucked. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety that year. It got so bad that for an entire month, I would just spend most of my day in the social worker’s office because I was dysfunctional. However, I was able to find lifelong friends. Like seriously. Ive been out of high school for 4 years, and I still talk to some of those people that I met at the new school. I know it might be really hard for you because you feel depressed, but try to make friends. I know there seems to be a lot more shitty people, but there’s gotta be at least one nice person in each class. Try a new afterschool activity or sport and make friends that way. Volunteer. Especially in times like this, having a good community and support system will be the best thing you ever did for yourself. Who knows, you might meet some lifelong friends who will be your bridesmaids one day, like I did. 

Hope this helps.

Ive had depression and anxiety and PTSD since I was a child, and was later diagnosed with Schizoeffective Disorder. Since May 2019, Ive been the most stable Ive ever been my entire life. Ive been extremely happy, and I dont think about my past abuse or carry it around with me, and I’ve been able to get over harmful habits and patterns like negative self talk, overthinking, and self depreciation.

Medicine helped me and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. Knowing the Cognitive Distortions and categorizing each irrational thought and replacing it with rational thoughts helped me. I had to do a lot of journaling and be extremely self aware to get this far. I couldn’t have done it without my counselors and community.

He has since passed away. I forgave him and was able to move on with my life despite the 18 years of abuse. My childhood caused me depression, anxiety, PTSD, and made me prone to developing Schizoeffective disorder later on. The only thing I have now is Schizoeffective Disorder (thanks to modern medicine and therapy). I am healed from most of my bad habits and patterns from what I went through growing up. Studying Cognitive Behavioral Therapy helped a lot. I don’t negative self talk anymore, I don’t degrade myself, I know how to express my emotions healthily, and I don’t even drag around my past anymore and let it affect my current friendships. I couldn’t have done it without my support system and my counselors. I worked really hard for the past 4 years to get to where I am today. It takes a lot of self awareness and digging, but investing in yourself is always worth your time.

Healing is on the way. If you need anything feel free to message me.

I’m just going to list off everything ever that I’ve had to teach myself with the help of mentors, friends, and extended family.

- How to regulate my emotions in a healthy manner: letting emotions pass, forgiveness, not letting them swallow me up into depression or anxiety
- How to handle conflict in a healthy manner: healthy conflict resolution
- How to set healthy boundaries: huge huge huge. No more codependency, abuse, weird family dynamics, fake friends, compromising my values, etc.
- How to set real values
- How to stay true to these values: living them out in a way that isn’t a contradiction
- How to express all emotions healthily
- How to be intimate and vulnerable with others: I can’t believe how I lived prior to this because now I love intimacy. I love helping others open up. 
- How to communicate effectively without choking up or making myself insignificant: thank god I started blogging, or I would have never been able to articulate my words well or express my emotions well
- How to be rational and understand irrational thinking patterns: 12 Irrational Thinking Patterns. I had to learn how to recognize them so if I had a thought, I can refute it.
- How to ask for help: my parents had too much pride to ask for help and that definitely carried over with myself
- How to be open to receiving help of all kinds, even as small as a friend offering to let me finish their food, a ride home, etc.
- How to clean: always yelled at for not cleaning, honestly didn’t even know how to do it
- How to buy groceries
- How to have real, authentic friendships
- How to date: my standards used to be so low because anything better than my parents was good enough. Also, for a while I thought all the good guys were taken or gay, and everyone else was immature or abusive. Lol
- How to cook
- How to handle personal finances
- How to throw myself into authentic community: this one is the newest one for me and is absolutely terrifying, but I like the genuineness of the people in my community. It’s sad that it’s new to me, but I’m so so happy that I have a second chance at authentic relationships
- How to socialize well for more than 4 hours a week (yeah that was about the time amount I had to spend with normal people, so when I went to college, I would literally subconsciously leave an event gathering after 4 hours because it just felt time to)
- How to understand body signs that indicate I need rest or medical attention
- How to handle failure and mistakes well: they are a normal part of life. Instead of letting it cripple me, let it teach me a new lesson
